text:
erin: heads-up — our telemetry shows ~1.3% of SSE clients get billed for two "start" events after a reconnect when the proxy's pingback/ack delay exceeds ~15s. console shows resume success but billing shows duplicate start. anyone seen this?

sam: can you paste an example trace or raw logs? is this specific to ws or sse?

erin: SSE. sample log (trimmed):
```
[proxy] 2026-02-12T14:02:11Z conn=tx123 resume_id=rid-9abc received resume
[proxy] 2026-02-12T14:02:27Z conn=tx123 session-start tenant=acme101
[billing] 2026-02-12T14:02:28Z charge start tenant=acme101 conn=tx123
[proxy] 2026-02-12T14:02:40Z conn=tx123 session-start tenant=acme101
[billing] 2026-02-12T14:02:41Z charge start tenant=acme101 conn=tx123
```
looks like proxy emitted start twice after a delayed pingback from backend. console only shows the resume ack (first one) so ops misses the duplicate billing.

julia: saw similar pattern during the keepalive timeout rollout yesterday. sticky routing + a slow backend pod caused a late health ping and the proxy retried the lease claim.

david: my hunch: resume idempotency isn't strictly enforced at the proxy edge — we treat a late health reply as a new session and re-emit session-start. billing just listens to session-start events, so duplicate.

sam: can we dedupe in billing by (tenant, resume_id)? do we have resume_id on billing events today?

erin: no, billing only gets connection id + tenant. resume_id isn't propagated through the event pipeline right now. console also doesn't surface resume_id on per-route traces which is part of the blind-spot.

console-eng: adding resume_id to the route-level trace payload is low-risk. would need a small schema bump in trace event and a quick console UI column. we can feature-flag it.

david: another mitigation: proxy holdback — when seeing a session-start for a conn with a resume_id seen in the last 30s, suppress duplicate start emission and emit a start-dedup telemetry tag. cheap fix.

sam: holdback seems reasonable but watch out for long GC windows; we already have TTLs on resume cache. what's a safe debounce? 5s? 30s?

erin: observed duplicates 13–45s apart in that sample. backend pingback variance is pretty wide. i'd vote for 60s debounce keyed by (tenant, resume_id) with a small memory footprint.

console-eng: note that a 60s debounce will change start-rate metrics and SLOs for live connections; we should add a migration note and a toggle so analytics teams can backfill.

david: agree. implementation plan: 1) quick proxy holdback feature-flagged 60s dedupe (edge), 2) add resume_id to telemetry pipeline + console column, 3) billing change to dedupe on resume_id once telemetry is live. canary deploy each step.

sam: who owns steps 1/2/3? i'm volunteer for billing changes (3). @erin can you take 1? console-eng take 2?

erin: i can pick up the proxy patch and a small e2e test. will create canary and wire deploy bot.

console-eng: will sketch the trace schema change and a tiny console card. feature-flagged behind `resume_trace_v1`.

julia: classify as sev3 — duplicate billing affects customers but has a clear mitigation path. i'll open a tracking incident and add runbook pointer.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: created canary release r-2026-02-12-proxy-dedupe-1 for eng-platform, target 2% traffic.

erin: thanks — opening PR/issue now: #4521. tagging @sam @david @console-eng. i'll drop a short repro script in the issue. :rocket:

sam: ack. keep me posted, i'll start billing-side patch draft.

julia: added incident-20260212 to oncall channel and pinned the console card request.

erin: quick repro curl for local testing (SSE resume header):
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Resume-ID: rid-9abc" "https://dev-api.redwood.inference/sse/stream?session=tx123"
# then simulate delayed backend heartbeat and reconnect
```

erin: any objections to the 60s holdback?
david: fine by me. roll it out behind flag and bump metric docs.

console-eng: no objections. will coordinate dashboards.

erin: great — i'll update thread with PR link and a quick canary result later. :thumbsup:
